A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FourierMamba work and are readable throughout. The original sections, equations, tables, and figures can be matched directly. v2 adds Figures 6–12 before the references; neither supplied PDF contains a separately labeled appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original deraining results in Table 1, component and scanning ablations in Tables 2–3, and qualitative restoration results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds amplitude-swapping examples and real-world deraining comparisons in Figures 7–12.

M1.justification: The FourierMamba architecture, spatial and channel scanning procedures, Fourier branches, and combined spatial/frequency loss remain unchanged in Sections 2.2–2.3.

E1.justification: Beyond the original Rain100H, Rain100L, Test2800, and Test1200 evaluations, Figures 9–12 add examples explicitly identified as real-world rain from RainDS-Real, Internet-Data, SPA-Data, and RE-RAIN. This substantially broadens represented evaluation conditions, although the additions are qualitative.

E2.justification: Existing comparisons retain their comparator sets. The new real-world comparisons reuse PreNet, MPRNet, and Restormer, already evaluated in v1. MAXIM also already appears in Figure 5; its appearance in the correction adds no new baseline.

E3.justification: The added real-world evaluation is visual-only: Figures 9 and 11 display ground truth, while Figures 10 and 12 provide comparisons without a displayed ground-truth reference. The original training schedule and Y-channel PSNR/SSIM protocol remain unchanged; further settings for the new evaluations are not documented.

E4.justification: Figures 7–8 extend the amplitude-swapping observation with additional cases, including real-world images, examining whether the frequency-domain degradation observation persists. The component, Fourier-prior, and scanning ablations in Tables 2–3 and Figure 4 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates for its results. The added figures introduce no statistical reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged. v2 adds selected real-world restoration and amplitude-swapping outcomes, plus a corrected MAXIM/Ours/GT display for the second Figure 5 example in Figure 6. These are qualitative additions and a localized correction, with no revised quantitative rankings.

T1.justification: The Fourier and state-space definitions, mathematical reasoning, and Equations 1–13 are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about Fourier-domain frequency correlation, scanning designs, and deraining performance.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and interpretations of the ablations remain unchanged. Figure 8 states that its additional examples align with the existing conclusion; it supplies supporting observations without introducing a new explanation, applicability qualification, or limitation.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same implementation details, including PyTorch, A100 hardware, block configuration, optimizer, and training schedule. The added figures provide no additional implementation, data-processing, checkpoint, or code/data-access information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 48 references are unchanged. The added figure captions name data sources without adding citations or changing the paper's positioning relative to previous methods.

P1.justification: v2 inserts a caption-led supplementary figure block between the conclusion and references and updates the version stamp. The existing prose, terminology, and section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 6–12 substantially expand the visual material with a correction panel, amplitude-swapping grids, and four real-world comparison grids. Figures 1–5 and the table structures remain unchanged; page 9 also receives tighter vertical spacing.

improvement.justification: The explicit Figure 5 correction and additional real-world and amplitude-swapping examples modestly improve transparency and empirical support. The gains are limited because the new evidence is qualitative and lacks accompanying evaluation details, while the original Figure 5 remains alongside its correction. The quantitative evidence and core claims are unchanged.
